_comment: Reference adult maximum daily doses for the demo dose-load check. These are widely published standard adult maximums, NOT personal medical advice and NOT a substitute for a pharmacist or doctor. Only drugs with a well-established single-number maximum are listed; drugs dosed by INR, weight or kidney function (e.g. warfarin) are deliberately absent, so the engine reports Unknown for them instead of inventing a limit. Add entries only with a citable source.

Amoxicillin.note: Usual adult maximum 3 g/day across indications.

Aspirin.note: Analgesic maximum. Low-dose antiplatelet use (75-100 mg) is far below this; the check is about total dose.

Caffeine.note: General adult guidance for total caffeine from all sources (medicines, tea, coffee).

Cetirizine.note: Standard adult dose is 10 mg once daily.

Ibuprofen.note: Over-the-counter limit. Prescription use can go higher under a doctor's direction — the engine uses the conservative OTC figure.

Loratadine.note: Standard adult dose is 10 mg once daily.

Metformin.note: Usual adult maximum 2,550 mg/day (immediate-release). Lower with kidney impairment — the engine does not know kidney function.

Omeprazole.note: Usual adult maximum 40 mg/day for common indications.

Paracetamol.note: Standard adult maximum 4 g/day from all sources combined, including combination products.

Simvastatin.note: Adult maximum 80 mg/day (the 80 mg dose itself carries extra muscle risk — flag, don't rely on this number alone).
